question: Can audits of one rollout per group identify the distribution of clean group-normalized GRPO advantages when verifier rewards are fixed but clean outcomes have different within-group dependence?
scope: Exact finite synthetic mechanism study. This is not language-model training or capability evidence.

worlds.A: For each group, draw Z ~ Bernoulli(0.5) and set clean labels to (Z,Z).
worlds.B: For each group, draw Z ~ Bernoulli(0.5) and set clean labels to (Z,1-Z).

observed_proxy: Every group has the same two members and proxy verifier labels (1,0). The auditor does not observe the un-audited clean labels.

audit_arms.item_uniform: Audit exactly one member per group, selected uniformly without replacement within that group; record member index and clean label.
audit_arms.item_proxy_positive: Audit member 0 per group, the member receiving proxy reward 1.
audit_arms.group_atomic: Audit both members of each sampled group; sample groups uniformly.

replicate_seeds: integers 0 through 1999 inclusive; Python random.Random(seed); no seed selection or replacement
primary_metrics: balanced accuracy for distinguishing a batch from world A versus world B using audited labels only
exact total-variation distance between the one-item audit observation laws in worlds A and B
secondary_metrics: within-group clean-label covariance estimate when jointly observed
advantage_definition: For binary rewards r=(r0,r1), use centered population-standardized advantages A_i=(r_i-mean(r))/sqrt(mean((r-mean(r))^2)); define A=(0,0) when variance is exactly zero.
trial_design: Each of the 2000 replicate seeds runs one batch from world A and one batch from world B. Each batch has a total budget of 200 clean-label calls. The item arms audit one member in each of 200 groups; the group arm audits both members in 100 groups. Balanced accuracy is computed across the 2000 batches for each world.

frozen_expectations.item_marginal_identifiability: Each member has marginal clean reward 0.5 in both worlds; member-index plus one audited label has the same distribution in both worlds, so no classifier using item-only audits can exceed balanced accuracy 0.5 in expectation, regardless of item-level propensity correction.
frozen_expectations.group_signal: World A always has A=(0,0); world B always has either (1,-1) or (-1,1). A complete audited group reveals whether its members agree.
frozen_expectations.decision_rule: Mechanism prediction is supported only if item-uniform and item-proxy-positive balanced accuracy are each <=0.55, group-atomic balanced accuracy is >=0.99, exact one-item observation-law TV is 0, and the independent audit reproduces all primary metrics. Otherwise report a non-pass without changing the protocol.

randomization: For each seed and world batch, independently draw group outcomes using random.Random(seed). For item_uniform, independently choose member 0/1 with that RNG. For world B, independently choose orientation Z for every group. Item-proxy-positive always audits member index 0. The item-only classifier predicts B iff audited label positives exceed half the batch; ties predict A. The group classifier predicts B iff any audited complete group is discordant.
limitations: The target is identifiability of the per-group normalized advantage signal, not the expected parameter update or downstream task success.
No language model, optimizer, or policy training is run.
The result does not establish that group-atomic audits are cost-optimal in general.
